mainTopic: When we can be sure a husband has died: identifying a body, a man lost in water with or without an end, and falls into dangerous pits.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a line from the previous page about why an attacker is not fully responsible for a death. Either the wind or the victim himself hurried it, and the גמרא shows a case where only one of these reasons applies. Next the גמרא asks whether רבי יהודה בן בבא disagrees with the three-day limit for identifying a body in order to be lenient or to be strict. Two drowning cases seem to prove he was lenient, but the גמרא answers that water is different: it keeps a body without a wound tight and recognizable, as long as it is seen right when it is pulled out. A new משנה rules that if a man falls into water and is not seen again, his wife may not remarry. רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי each bring stories to illustrate. The ברייתא shows that the חכמים permit the wife when the water has an end, meaning all its shores can be seen, and אביי defines that term. The story of רב שילא, who wrongly permitted a wife in the lake of סמקי, and several survival stories, including רבי עקיבא and רבי מאיר at sea, show why the rule for water with no end is strict. The amud ends with a ברייתא about a man who fell into a lions' den or a pit of snakes, and רבי יהודה בן בתירא's reason for his opinion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: What difference is there between the two reasons?
steps.stepSummary: The line from the previous page ends: '...or he himself hastened his death.' The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between that reason and the wind reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: '...or he himself hastened his death.' What is the difference between these two reasons?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a statement from the previous page and then asks a clarifying question. It wants to know when the two reasons would actually lead to different results.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two reasons were given for why the attacker is not held responsible for the death. One is that the wind may have hurried the death, and the other is that the victim may have hurried it himself. If both reasons usually apply together, why mention both? The גמרא is looking for a case where only one of them applies.

keyTerms.meaning: He hastened (brought closer) his own death
What is the difference between them? (a standard question asking for a practical difference)

phrases.english: ...hastened his death.
phrases.notes: This finishes a line from the previous page: either the wind hurried his death, or he himself did.

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the end of a statement from the previous page and asks how its two reasons differ.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where the 'wind' reason and the 'he hastened his own death' reason give different results.

steps.title: Marble house versus open field
steps.stepSummary: The difference shows up in two cases. In a closed marble house there is no wind, but the victim thrashed. Outdoors there is wind, but the victim did not thrash.
steps.simpleTranslation: One case is where he cut him in a closed marble house and the victim convulsed. Another case is where he cut him outside and the victim did not convulse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with two cases. In each one, only one of the two reasons applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a sealed marble house there is no wind, but the victim thrashed. Under the 'he hastened his own death' reason the attacker is not held responsible, but under the wind reason he would be. Outdoors with no thrashing it is the other way around, so the two explanations lead to different results in these cases.

keyTerms.meaning: A house of marble: a fully closed room with no wind
Outside, out in the open field

steps.whatToRemember: The two reasons give different results. No wind but thrashing: only 'he hastened it' frees the attacker. Wind but no thrashing: only the wind reason frees him.

phrases.english: Where one cut him in a house of marble
and he convulsed.
Alternatively:
where one cut him outside
and he did not convulse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of what difference there is between the two reasons.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No wind but thrashing means only 'he hastened his death' applies. Wind but no thrashing means only the wind reason applies.

steps.title: Is רבי יהודה בן בבא more lenient or more strict?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's 'not every person, place, or time is the same' from רבי יהודה בן בבא. It asks whether he means to permit testimony even after three days, or to forbid it even within three days.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: 'Not every... etc.' A question was asked: does רבי יהודה בן בבא disagree in order to be lenient, or in order to be strict?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting the משנה. It then asks which direction רבי יהודה בן בבא's disagreement goes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling in the משנה is that you may identify a body only within three days of death. 'Not every person, place, or time is the same' could cut either way. Sometimes a body stays recognizable longer, which would be lenient. Sometimes it changes faster, which would be strict.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them (a real open question)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume 'not every case is the same' must mean 'more lenient.' The words fit both directions, and that is exactly why the גמרא asks.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: לֹא כָּל וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: Not every, etc.
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה: not every person, every place, or every time is the same.

phrases.english: A question was asked of them:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בָּבָא לְקוּלָּא פְּלִיג,
phrases.english: Does Rabbi Yehuda ben Bava disagree to be lenient,
or does he disagree to be strict?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of the attacker and turns to a new line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי יהודה בן בבא's 'not every case is the same' allows testimony beyond three days or forbids it even within three days.

steps.title: A drowned man found after three days
steps.stepSummary: A man drowned in כרמי and was pulled out after three days. רב דימי מנהרדעא allowed his wife to remarry.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: a certain man drowned in כרמי, and they pulled him out at בי הדיא after three days, and רב דימי of נהרדעא allowed his wife to remarry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a real case to try to answer the question. It shows a body identified after more than three days, and the wife was still permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling in the משנה limits identification to three days. Here the identification came after three days and was still accepted. That suggests the lenient reading of רבי יהודה בן בבא, where some cases allow more time.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (introducing a source to answer a question)
They brought him up / pulled him out
He married off his wife, meaning he permitted her to remarry

phrases.english: Come and hear:
that a certain man drowned in Carmi,
and they pulled him out at Bei Hedya
after three days,
and Rav Dimi of Nehardea allowed his wife to marry.
phrases.notes: Literally 'he married off his wife.' רב דימי ruled that she was a widow and free to remarry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a real case to try to settle the lenient-or-strict question.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה בן בבא disagrees to be lenient, allowing identification after three days.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב דימי מנהרדעא's actual ruling permitting the wife after the body was found three days later.

steps.title: A second drowned man found after five days
steps.stepSummary: A man drowned in the דגלת and was pulled out onto the bridge of שביסתנא. רבא allowed his wife to remarry based on his groomsmen's identification, five days after death.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore: a certain man drowned in the דגלת, and they pulled him out onto the bridge of שביסתנא, and רבא allowed his wife to remarry based on the word of his groomsmen, after five days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second case to strengthen the first. This time even five days passed, and the wife was still permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This case goes even further past the three-day limit than the first one, which makes the lenient direction look stronger. The identifiers were his groomsmen, people who knew him very well. The two cases together point toward reading רבי יהודה בן בבא as lenient.

keyTerms.meaning: Groomsmen: close friends from the wedding

steps.whyThisMatters: These cases show real rabbis permitting an עגונה to remarry even after the three-day limit. That matters a great deal for practical הלכה about freeing a woman whose husband drowned.

phrases.english: And furthermore:
a certain man drowned in the Tigris,
and they pulled him out onto the bridge of Shabistana,
and Rava allowed his wife to marry
based on the word of the groomsmen
after five days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, even stronger case to the proof from step 4.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה בן בבא disagrees to be lenient.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבא's ruling permitting the wife based on the groomsmen's identification five days after death.

steps.title: The drowning stories seem to show רבי יהודה בן בבא was lenient
steps.stepSummary: If רבי יהודה בן בבא was being lenient, the rulings of רב דימי and רבא follow him. If he was being strict, whose opinion did they follow?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense if you say he argued in order to be lenient: then those rabbis who allowed the women to remarry acted like רבי יהודה בן בבא. But if you say he argued in order to be strict, whose opinion did they follow?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the two drowning stories from Steps 4 and 5 to answer its question from Step 3. They seem to prove that רבי יהודה בן בבא meant to be lenient.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב דימי and רבא both accepted identification of a body that had been dead for three or more days. That only fits a view that permits testimony after three days. If רבי יהודה בן בבא was being strict, nobody would support these rulings.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense, granted (sets up 'this works, but that doesn't')

phrases.english: It makes sense if you say he disagreed to be lenient:
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבי יהודה בן בבא, from the משנה quoted in Step 3.

phrases.aramaic: אִינְהוּ דַּעֲבוּד כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בָּבָא.
phrases.english: then those who acted did so like רבי יהודה בן בבא.
But if you say he disagreed to be strict,
then whose opinion did those who acted follow?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the stories in Steps 4 and 5
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה בן בבא meant to permit testimony even after three days
steps.raayaSupportSource: The rulings of רב דימי מנהרדעא and רבא about drowned men

steps.title: Water is different because it shrinks the body
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed away: the cases involved water, and water keeps the body from changing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Water is different, because it shrinks the body.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from Step 6. Those cases were drownings, and water is a special situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The usual worry is that a body's face changes after three days. Water tightens the body, so the face stays recognizable longer. So the stories can work even if רבי יהודה בן בבא was being strict on dry land.

phrases.english: Water is different, since it contracts the body.
phrases.notes: Because the body tightens instead of swelling, the face doesn't change shape.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in Step 6
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from the drowning stories; the question about רבי יהודה בן בבא stays open
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The stories were about water, which keeps a body recognizable, so they say nothing about ordinary cases

steps.title: But we said water makes a wound worse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges Step 7: earlier it said water aggravates a wound, so water does not always help.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't you say that water makes a wound worse?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that water shrinks the body. It points to an earlier statement that water makes wounds swell.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If water causes swelling around a wound, how can we say water keeps the body tight? The two statements seem to contradict each other.

phrases.english: But didn't you say that water aggravates a wound?!
phrases.notes: This points back to a statement on the previous page (120b).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the claim made in Step 7
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that water shrinks the body
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An earlier statement says water makes wounds swell, which contradicts the idea that water keeps the body tight

steps.title: Water swells a wound, but shrinks a body with no wound
steps.stepSummary: Both statements are true: water makes a wound swell, but where there is no wound it tightens the body.
steps.simpleTranslation: That applies where there is a wound. But where there is no wound, the water definitely tightens the body.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by splitting the cases. Wound means swelling, no wound means shrinking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier statement was only about a wounded body. A body without a wound is tightened by water, so the face keeps its shape, and the answer in Step 7 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: These words apply only (to a certain case)

phrases.english: This applies where there is a wound,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הֵיכָא דְּלֵיכָּא מַכָּה — מִיצְמָת צָמֵית.
phrases.english: but where there is no wound, it definitely contracts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 8
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Water always makes a body swell, so a drowned face cannot be recognized
steps.terutzMaskana: Water swells only a wound; a body with no wound is tightened and stays recognizable

steps.title: Only if the body is seen right after it is pulled out
steps.stepSummary: The water helps only if the body is identified right when it comes out. If they wait, it swells up.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this applies only when they pulled him out and saw him right away. But if they waited, the body certainly swells up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a limit to the water rule. Identification must happen right when the body is taken out of the water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Water keeps the body tight only while it is in the water. Once it is out, the body quickly swells and becomes hard to recognize. So testimony after a delay is not trusted.
steps.whatToRemember: Water explains the drowning stories: a body without a wound stays recognizable in water, but only if it is identified right when it is pulled out.

phrases.english: And this applies when they pulled him out
and saw him at that time.
But if it was delayed, it definitely swells.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָנֵי מִילֵּי דְּכִי אַסְּקֵיהּ חַזְיֵיהּ בְּשַׁעְתֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Puts a limit on the rule from Step 9
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A drowned body can be identified only if it is seen right when it is taken out of the water

steps.title: A man who fell into water: his wife may not remarry
steps.stepSummary: New משנה: if a man fell into water and was not seen again, his wife may not remarry, whatever the size of the water.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a man fell into water, whether or not you can see where the water ends, his wife is forbidden to remarry.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It rules that falling into water and disappearing is not enough proof of death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if the water has visible edges, he may have climbed out somewhere without being seen. Since there is no sure proof he died, his wife stays married.
steps.confusionAlert: Water 'with an end' means you can see all its edges. You might think that is proof he died, since nobody saw him come out. The משנה says even then she may not remarry.

phrases.english: MISHNA: If he fell into water,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶן סוֹף, בֵּין שֶׁאֵין לָהֶן סוֹף —
phrases.english: whether the water has an end or has no end,
his wife is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָפַל לְמַיִם, בֵּין שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶן סוֹף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A man who fell into any water and was not seen again is not assumed dead; his wife may not remarry

steps.title: רבי מאיר: a man came out of a pit after three days
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר tells of a man who fell into a large pit and came up alive after three days.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר said: There was a case of a man who fell into the great pit and came up after three days.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר supports the strict ruling with a true story. People can survive even when everyone thinks they are dead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This man was gone for three days, long enough that anyone would assume he drowned. Yet he came out alive. So disappearing in water does not prove death.

keyTerms.meaning: A true incident, a case that happened

phrases.english: רבי מאיר said:
There was an incident with one who fell into the great pit,
and came up after three days.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּאֶחָד שֶׁנָּפַל לְבוֹר הַגָּדוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the ruling of Step 11 with a story
steps.raayaObject: That a man who disappears in water may still be alive
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of the man who came out of the great pit after three days

steps.title: רבי יוסי: the blind man and his guide in the cave
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי tells of a blind man and his guide who went into a cave to immerse and stayed under too long to survive. Their wives were allowed to remarry.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: There was a case of a blind man who went down to immerse in a cave, and his guide went down after him. They stayed there long enough to die, and the rabbis allowed their wives to remarry.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי brings a story where the wives were allowed to remarry. It shows that sometimes a disappearance in water is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the water was a contained pool in a cave, and they stayed under long enough to die. Had they come out, they would have been seen, so the rabbis treated them as dead. This seems to go against the strict ruling of the משנה, at least in a case like this.

keyTerms.meaning: To immerse in water for purity
His guide (the one who leads him)

phrases.english: רבי יוסי said:
There was an incident with a blind man who went down to immerse in a cave,
and his guide went down after him,
and they stayed long enough for their souls to leave,
and they allowed their wives to marry.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּסוֹמֵא שֶׁיָּרַד לִטְבּוֹל בִּמְעָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a story where the outcome was lenient, unlike רבי מאיר's story
steps.raayaObject: That in some water cases, the wives may remarry
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of the blind man and his guide in the cave

steps.title: The man in עסיא whose leg came back: above or below the knee
steps.stepSummary: A man was lowered into the sea and only his leg came back. The חכמים ruled: cut above the knee, his wife may remarry; below the knee, she may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another case happened in עסיא: they lowered a man into the sea, and only his leg came back up in their hands. The חכמים said: if it was cut from the knee and up, she may marry. From the knee and down, she may not marry.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי brings a second story. The rabbis decided by where the leg was cut.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person cannot survive losing his leg above the knee, so he is surely dead. If it was cut below the knee he might have lived, so his wife stays married. Death is accepted only when it is certain.

keyTerms.meaning: A place name (often linked to Asia Minor)
They lowered him down (on a rope)

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה rules that disappearing into water is not proof of death. רבי מאיר backs this with a survivor story, while רבי יוסי shows cases where death was clear enough to let the wives remarry.

phrases.english: And again, an incident in עסיא,
with one whom they lowered into the sea,
and only his leg came up in their hands.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ חֲכָמִים: מִן הָאַרְכּוּבָּה וּלְמַעְלָה — תִּנָּשֵׂא.
phrases.english: The חכמים said: From the knee and above, she may marry.
phrases.notes: He means the leg was cut off above the knee, a wound nobody survives.

phrases.english: From the knee and below, she may not marry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second story from רבי יוסי, continuing Step 13
steps.raayaObject: That a wife may remarry when death is certain from the evidence
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story in עסיא and the חכמים's knee rule

steps.title: רבי מאיר and the חכמים argue about water with and without an end
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: רבי מאיר forbids the wife in all water. The חכמים permit her when the water has a visible end and forbid her when it has no end.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: If a man fell into water, whether the water has an end or has no end, his wife is forbidden to remarry. That is the view of רבי מאיר. The חכמים say: if the water has an end, his wife is permitted. If the water has no end, his wife is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a מחלוקת about our משנה's case: a man fell into water and was never seen coming out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר says we can never assume he died, because he may have come up somewhere unseen. The חכמים split the case. If the edges can be seen, anyone who climbed out would have been noticed, so he surely drowned. If the edges cannot be seen, he may have gotten out somewhere out of view.

keyTerms.meaning: Water with a visible end or shore

steps.confusionAlert: Even the חכמים forbid her in water with no end. They only argue with רבי מאיר about water whose edges can be seen.
steps.whyThisMatters: This split between the two kinds of water is the key idea for everything that follows, including the story of רב שילא.

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Sages taught:
If a man fell into the water,
whether it has an end,
phrases.notes: "End" means you can see the shore, so someone climbing out would be noticed.

phrases.english: or it does not have an end —
his wife is forbidden; these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
And the Sages say:

phrases.aramaic: מַיִם שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶם סוֹף — אִשְׁתּוֹ מוּתֶּרֶת,
phrases.english: Water that has an end — his wife is permitted,
and water that has no end — his wife is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that adds a מחלוקת to the משנה's case in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: forbidden in all water. חכמים: permitted when the water has an end, forbidden when it has no end.

steps.title: What counts as water with an end?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how to define water that has an end.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case of water that has an end?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a definition of the term the חכמים used. It is setting up אביי's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling of the חכמים depends on this term, so it needs a clear measure. Otherwise a בית דין would not know which lakes allow the wife to remarry.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? How do we picture it?

phrases.aramaic: הֵיכִי דָּמֵי מַיִם שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶם סוֹף?
phrases.english: What is the case of water that has an end?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a definition of a term used by the חכמים in step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How to define מים שיש להם סוף.

steps.title: אביי: you can see the shore on all four sides
steps.stepSummary: אביי: water has an end if a person standing there can see the shore in all four directions.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Any water where a person stands and can see its edges in all four directions.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question by giving a clear test for water with an end.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a person can see every edge from one spot, a man who climbed out anywhere would have been seen. If any side is out of view, he could have come out there unnoticed. In that case the water counts as having no end.
steps.whatToRemember: Water with an end is water whose shores can all be seen from where the man fell in. Only there do the חכמים let the wife remarry.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Any water where one stands and sees on all four of its sides.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Water counts as having an end if one can see its shores on all four sides.

steps.title: רב שילא permits a wife, and רב wants to put him in נידוי
steps.stepSummary: A man drowned in the lake of סמקי, and רב שילא let his wife remarry. רב wanted to put רב שילא in נידוי. שמואל said to send him a question first.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a man who drowned in the lake of סמקי, and רב שילא allowed his wife to marry. רב said to שמואל: Come, let us put him in נידוי. שמואל said to him: Let us first send him a message.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real case where a רב let a wife remarry after her husband drowned in a lake. It is setting up the questions that are sent to him next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב saw this ruling as a serious mistake, strong enough to deserve נידוי. שמואל wanted to hear רב שילא's side before acting.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us put him in נידוי (a ban)

phrases.english: There was a certain man who drowned in the lake of Samkei,
and Rav Sheila allowed his wife to marry.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב לִשְׁמוּאֵל, תָּא נְשַׁמְּתֵיהּ.
phrases.english: Rav said to Shmuel: Come, let us put him in a ban.
He said to him: Let us send to him first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a real case that tests the rule of the חכמים and אביי's definition.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב שילא permitted the wife of a man who drowned in the lake of סמקי. רב objected strongly.

steps.title: First question to רב שילא: what is the law in endless water?
steps.stepSummary: They ask רב שילא whether the wife is forbidden or permitted when her husband disappears in endless water.
steps.simpleTranslation: They sent to him: Water that has no end, is his wife forbidden or permitted?
steps.whatsHappening: רב and שמואל send רב שילא a question to check whether he knows the basic rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before judging him, they want to know whether he made a mistake in the הלכה itself. They start with the general rule.

phrases.english: They sent to him:

phrases.aramaic: מַיִם שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם סוֹף, אִשְׁתּוֹ אֲסוּרָה אוֹ מוּתֶּרֶת?
phrases.english: Water that has no end, is his wife forbidden or permitted?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Carries out שמואל's plan to send a question first.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רב שילא agrees that the wife is forbidden in endless water.

steps.title: רב שילא: in endless water, the wife is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רב שילא answers that in endless water the wife is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: He sent to them: His wife is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שילא answers that he agrees with the standard rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So his ruling was not a mistake about the basic law. This shifts the question to the facts: what kind of water is this lake?

phrases.english: He sent to them: His wife is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: In water with no end, the wife is forbidden.

steps.title: Second question: is the lake of סמקי endless water?
steps.stepSummary: They ask whether the lake of סמקי is water with an end or without an end.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the lake of סמקי: is it water that has an end, or water that has no end?
steps.whatsHappening: They send a second question, this time about the facts of this specific lake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב שילא knows the rule, so maybe he thought this lake has a visible end. This question checks that.

phrases.english: And the lake of Samkei —

phrases.aramaic: מַיִם שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶם סוֹף, אוֹ מַיִם שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם סוֹף?
phrases.english: is it water that has an end, or water that has no end?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After he agreed to the rule, they ask about the facts.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the lake of סמקי is water with an end.

steps.title: רב שילא: the lake of סמקי has no end
steps.stepSummary: רב שילא answers that the lake of סמקי is water with no end.
steps.simpleTranslation: He sent to them: It is water that has no end.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שילא admits that this lake counts as endless water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By his own answers, the rule should forbid the wife. That makes his ruling even harder to understand.

phrases.english: He sent to them:
It is water that has no end.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַח לְהוּ: מַיִם שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם סוֹף הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The lake of סמקי is water with no end.

steps.title: So why did רב שילא permit her?
steps.stepSummary: They ask רב שילא: if so, what was your reason for ruling this way?
steps.simpleTranslation: And the Master, what is the reason he acted this way?
steps.whatsHappening: After both answers, they challenge רב שילא: by your own words she should be forbidden, so why did you permit her? The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His two answers together lead to "forbidden," yet he ruled "permitted." The question presses him to explain what other reason he relied on.

keyTerms.meaning: The Master (a polite way to address a חכם)

phrases.english: And the Master, what is the reason he acted this way?
phrases.notes: "The Master" is רב שילא. They are speaking to him politely.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רב שילא's two answers to challenge his ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב שילא's ruling permitting the wife of the man who drowned in the lake of סמקי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: He agrees that endless water forbids the wife, and that this lake is endless water. So his ruling seems to contradict his own words.

steps.title: רב שילא admits his mistake about the lake
steps.stepSummary: רב שילא explains that he mistakenly treated the still lake of סמקי as water with an end. Because it has waves, the man could have been carried out of sight and still be alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: I made a mistake. I thought that since the water is gathered and still, it is like water with an end. But that is not right: since there are waves, we must say the waves carried him away out of sight.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שילא answers the question of why he ruled as he did: he admits he simply made an error.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His reasoning was that still, non-flowing water is like a body of water whose edges you can see. The flaw is that this lake has waves. Waves can carry a person beyond where we can see, so he may have come out alive, and the wife must stay forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: carried him away / pushed him out of sight

phrases.english: I made a mistake,
I thought:
since the waters are gathered and standing still,
they are like water that has an end.
But that is not so:
since there are waves,
say that the waves carried him away.
phrases.notes: The waves could have moved him past where anyone could see, so he may have climbed out alive somewhere else.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 23 about his reasoning by admitting an error.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רב שילא ruled leniently about the lake of סמקי.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He mistakenly treated still water as water with an end. Because of the waves, it is really water with no end.

steps.title: רב and שמואל praise each other with verses
steps.stepSummary: שמואל applies a פסוק to רב, saying no harm came to the righteous. רב applies a פסוק to שמואל about the value of good advice.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל read this verse about רב: "No mischief shall befall the righteous." רב read this verse about שמואל: "Salvation comes through much counsel."
steps.whatsHappening: The story of רב שילא closes with רב and שמואל praising each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רב שילא had only made an honest mistake, it would have been unjust to punish him. שמואל says the righteous רב was protected from doing that wrong. רב credits שמואל's advice to ask רב שילא first, which led to this good outcome.

keyTerms.meaning: no harm will come to the righteous

phrases.english: Shmuel read this verse about Rav:
"No mischief shall befall the righteous."
Rav read this verse about Shmuel:
"But salvation lies in much counsel."

steps.whatToRemember: The lake of סמקי, even though it is still, counts as water with no end because of its waves. רב שילא's lenient ruling was an honest mistake.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the רב שילא story after his admission.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The patience to check before punishing prevented an injustice.

steps.title: The fisherman in the fish cave in the Jordan
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא tells of a man thought drowned in the ירדן who was really alive in a fish cave. רבי uses this to praise the חכמים' rule forbidding the wife when the water has no end.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי said: Two men were fishing with nets in the ירדן. One went into a fish cave. The sun set, and he could not see the way out. His friend waited long enough for him to have died, then went and told his family. The next day the sun rose, the man found the opening, came home, and found a great eulogy going on. רבי said: How great are the words of the חכמים, who said that in water with an end the wife is permitted, but in water with no end she is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a real-life story that shows why the חכמים' rule about endless water makes sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone was sure the man had drowned, yet he was alive in a hidden cave. This shows that when the water has no end, a person can disappear from sight and still survive. So the חכמים rightly forbid his wife to remarry.

keyTerms.meaning: a fish cave (an underwater hollow where fish gather)
(long enough) for his soul to leave, meaning for him to die

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi said:
There was an incident with two people
who were fishing with nets in the Jordan,
and one of them went into
a fish cave,
and the sun set,
and he could not see the cave's opening,
and his friend waited long enough for his soul to have left him,
and he came and told his household.
The next day, the sun rose,
and he recognized the cave's opening,

phrases.aramaic: וּבָא וּמָצָא הֶסְפֵּד גָּדוֹל בְּתוֹךְ בֵּיתוֹ.
phrases.english: and he came and found a great eulogy in his house.
Rabbi said:
How great are the words of the Sages, who said:
water that has an end:
his wife is permitted;
water that has no end:
his wife is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי: מַעֲשֶׂה בִּשְׁנֵי בְּנֵי אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the rule that in water with no end the wife is forbidden.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a wife is forbidden when her husband disappears in water with no end.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story in the ברייתא of the fisherman in the ירדן who survived in a fish cave.

steps.title: Why not worry about a fish cave in water with an end too
steps.stepSummary: If a person can survive hidden in a fish cave, the same worry should apply even in water with an end.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, even in water that has an end, we should worry that he is hiding in a fish cave!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the lenient half of the rule, using the story it just told.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story shows a man can stay hidden in a cave and be wrongly thought dead. If so, even when we can see all the edges of the water, maybe he is inside an underwater cave. Then the wife should be forbidden there too.

phrases.english: If so,
in water that has an end too,
let us be concerned about a fish cave!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, מַיִם שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶם סוֹף נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the story from step 26 to attack the leniency in water with an end.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that the wife is permitted when the water has an end.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The fish-cave possibility would seem to exist in any water, so the leniency should not hold.

steps.title: Fish caves are uncommon in water with an end
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that fish caves are not common in water with an end, so we do not worry about them there.
steps.simpleTranslation: In water that has an end, fish caves are not common.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by pointing to how often such caves actually occur.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We only worry about realistic possibilities. In large, endless water like the ירדן, such caves are found. In water with an end, they are rare, so the leniency stays in place.

phrases.english: In water that has an end,
a fish cave is not common.

steps.whatToRemember: Water with an end: the wife is permitted, because fish caves there are rare. Water with no end: the wife is forbidden, because he may have been carried away or be hidden alive.
steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַיִם שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶם סוֹף מְחִילָּה שֶׁל דָּגִים לָא שְׁכִיחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases by how common the risk is
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The fish-cave worry applies equally to all water, so the wife should be forbidden even in water with an end.
steps.terutzMaskana: Fish caves are uncommon in water with an end, so we do not worry about them, and the wife is permitted.

steps.title: רב אשי: A Torah scholar would be known if he survived
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the rule forbidding the wife when the water has no end applies only to an ordinary person. If a צורבא מרבנן came out alive, people would hear about it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: When the רבנן said that if a man fell into water with no end his wife is forbidden, that is only about an ordinary person. A young Torah scholar is different. If he came out of the water, word would spread.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי suggests an exception to the rule that a wife is forbidden when her husband fell into water with no end. He says a Torah scholar is not included.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We forbid the wife because the husband may have come out somewhere out of sight and still be alive. רב אשי argues that a known scholar cannot disappear quietly. If he survived, people would talk about it, so his silence suggests he really died.

keyTerms.meaning: It would be heard about; word would spread
This applies only to... (limits a rule)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: הָא דַּאֲמַרוּ רַבָּנַן
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: That which the Rabbis said,

phrases.aramaic: מַיִם שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם סוֹף אִשְׁתּוֹ אֲסוּרָה —
phrases.english: water with no end, his wife is forbidden —
this applies only to an ordinary person,
but a Torah scholar — no.
phrases.notes: So if a scholar fell into such water, his wife would be allowed to remarry.

phrases.english: If he had come up, there would be talk of it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: הָא דַּאֲמַרוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the discussion of water with and without an end, רב אשי suggests an exception to the strict rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ban on remarriage when the water has no end applies only to an ordinary person, not to a Torah scholar, because a scholar's survival would become known.

steps.title: No difference between scholar and ordinary person
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רב אשי. The rule is the same for everyone: after the fact the remarriage stands, but she may not remarry in the first place.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is not so. It makes no difference whether he is an ordinary person or a Torah scholar. If she already remarried, yes, she may stay married. To begin with, no, she may not remarry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects רב אשי's exception and applies the same rule to everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא does not accept that a scholar's fame removes the worry. For both kinds of people it gives one rule. If she already married, we leave her married. We do not allow her to marry in the first place.

keyTerms.meaning: But that is not so (a rejection)
After the fact, once it already happened
In the first place, from the start

steps.whatToRemember: Water with no end: a scholar and an ordinary person are treated alike. If the wife already remarried, she may stay married. She may not remarry in the first place.
steps.confusionAlert: The דיעבד/לכתחילה rule here is about the case of water with no end. It does not mean the wife may freely remarry. She is still forbidden to marry in the first place.

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא הִיא: לָא שְׁנָא אִינִישׁ דְּעָלְמָא,
phrases.english: But that is not so: there is no difference for an ordinary person,
and no difference for a Torah scholar;
after the fact — yes, in the first place — no.
phrases.notes: If she already remarried she may stay with her new husband, but she should not remarry to begin with.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא הִיא: לָא שְׁנָא אִינִישׁ דְּעָלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the exception רב אשי proposed in step 29.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole distinction between a Torah scholar and an ordinary person.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A scholar's fame does not change the law. Everyone gets the same rule: the remarriage stands after the fact, but she may not remarry in the first place.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Same rule for everyone: valid after the fact, forbidden in the first place.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל sees רבי עקיבא survive a shipwreck
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: רבן גמליאל saw a ship break apart and mourned רבי עקיבא, who was on it. Later רבי עקיבא showed up alive. He had held onto a plank and ducked his head under each wave.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבן גמליאל said: Once I was traveling on a ship, and I saw a ship that broke apart. I was sad about the Torah scholar on it, רבי עקיבא. When I reached dry land, he came, sat, and discussed הלכה with me. I said: My son, who brought you up? He said: A plank from the ship came my way, and I bowed my head to every wave that came at me.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story showing that someone lost at sea can really survive. This sets up רבן גמליאל's praise of the חכמים' rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא's ship was destroyed in open sea, which is water with no end, and anyone would have thought he was dead. Yet he was alive. This shows the real danger of letting a wife remarry in such a case.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
Who brought you up (out of the water)?

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabban Gamliel said:
Once I was traveling on a ship,
and I saw a ship that broke apart.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָיִיתִי מִצְטַעֵר עַל תַּלְמִיד חָכָם שֶׁבָּהּ,
phrases.english: And I was grieving over the Torah scholar who was on it,
and who was it? Rabbi Akiva.
And when I got onto dry land,
he came, and sat, and discussed halakha before me.
I said to him: My son, who brought you up?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לִי: דַּף שֶׁל סְפִינָה נִזְדַּמֵּן לִי,
phrases.english: He said to me: A plank of the ship came my way,
and each and every wave that came at me —
I bowed my head to it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל: פַּעַם אַחַת הָיִיתִי מְהַלֵּךְ בִּסְפִינָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to supporting the main rule about water with no end, like the ירדן story in step 26.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a wife is forbidden when her husband fell into water with no end.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recording רבן גמליאל's own experience with רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: Side lesson: bow your head before the wicked
steps.stepSummary: From רבי עקיבא's ducking under the waves, the חכמים learned that when wicked people come against a person, he should bow his head before them.
steps.simpleTranslation: From here the חכמים said: If wicked people come against a person, he should bow his head to them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses the story to draw a life lesson from how רבי עקיבא survived the waves. Then the story continues.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as ducking under each wave kept רבי עקיבא from being swept away, giving way for a moment before wicked people can save a person. This is a side point, not part of the law about the wife.

keyTerms.meaning: From here they said (a lesson drawn from the story)
He should bow his head (give way for the moment)

steps.confusionAlert: This line interrupts the story. The next line, אמרתי באותה שעה, is still רבן גמליאל speaking about the הלכה.

phrases.english: From here the Sages said:
If wicked people come upon a person —
he should bow his head to them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side lesson drawn from the end of רבי עקיבא's answer in step 31.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When wicked people come against you, give way for the moment, as רבי עקיבא did with the waves.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל praises the חכמים' rule
steps.stepSummary: Back in the story, רבן גמליאל says that at that moment he saw how great the חכמים' words were: water with an end, the wife is allowed; water with no end, she is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: I said at that moment: How great are the words of the חכמים, who said: water with an end, she is allowed; water with no end, she is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל finishes his story by saying it proves the חכמים' rule correct.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Had רבי עקיבא's wife been allowed to remarry because his ship was destroyed, it would have been a disaster, since he was alive. His survival in open sea shows why the חכמים forbid the wife when the water has no end.

keyTerms.meaning: How great are the words of the Sages

phrases.english: I said at that moment:
phrases.notes: This is רבן גמליאל speaking again, back in his story.

phrases.english: How great are the words of the Sages, who said:
water with an end — she is permitted,
water with no end — she is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַרְתִּי בְּאוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה: כַּמָּה גְּדוֹלִים דִּבְרֵי חֲכָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the side lesson in step 32 and finishes the story from step 31.
steps.raayaObject: The difference between water with an end and water with no end.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי עקיבא survived in open sea, though everyone thought he had drowned.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא sees רבי מאיר survive at sea
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא: רבי עקיבא saw a ship being tossed at sea and mourned רבי מאיר, who was on it. Later רבי מאיר appeared in קפוטקיא. One wave passed him to the next until he was thrown onto dry land. רבי עקיבא praises the חכמים' rule in the same words.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי עקיבא said: Once I was traveling on a ship, and I saw a ship being tossed at sea. I was sad about the Torah scholar on it, רבי מאיר. When I reached the land of קפוטקיא, he came, sat, and discussed הלכה with me. I said: My son, who brought you up? He said: One wave pushed me to the next, and that one to the next, until it threw me up onto dry land. I said at that moment: How great are the words of the חכמים, who said: water with an end, his wife is allowed; water with no end, his wife is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second, very similar story, this time with רבי עקיבא as the witness and רבי מאיר as the survivor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי מאיר's telling, the waves themselves passed him along, one to the next, until one threw him onto dry land. That is exactly the worry with water that has no end: the man can be carried out of sight and still be alive.
steps.whatToRemember: Two great scholars, רבי עקיבא and רבי מאיר, were thought drowned at sea and turned out to be alive. Each time the witness praised the חכמים' rule: water with no end, the wife is forbidden.
steps.whyThisMatters: These stories show that the strict rule for water with no end is not just theory. People really are carried far away by the sea and survive.

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Akiva said:
Once I was traveling on a ship,
and I saw a ship being tossed about at sea,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָיִיתִי מִצְטַעֵר עַל תַּלְמִיד חָכָם שֶׁבָּהּ,
phrases.english: and I was grieving over the Torah scholar who was on it,
and who was it? Rabbi Meir.
When I got off in the land of Cappadocia,
he came, and sat, and discussed halakha before me.
I said to him: My son, who brought you up?
He said to me: A wave pushed me to the next one,
and that one to the next, until it threw me up onto dry land.
I said at that moment:
How great are the words of the Sages, who said:

phrases.aramaic: מַיִם שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶם סוֹף — אִשְׁתּוֹ מוּתֶּרֶת,
phrases.english: water with an end — his wife is permitted,

phrases.aramaic: מַיִם שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם סוֹף — אִשְׁתּוֹ אֲסוּרָה.
phrases.english: water with no end — his wife is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: פַּעַם אַחַת הָיִיתִי מְהַלֵּךְ בִּסְפִינָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second story built just like רבן גמליאל's, adding more support for the same rule.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a wife is forbidden when her husband fell into water with no end.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recording רבי עקיבא's own experience with רבי מאיר, who was carried by waves to a faraway land.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Survival in open sea really happens, so the חכמים were right to forbid the wife when the water has no end.

steps.title: Lions' den versus a pit of snakes and scorpions
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that falling into a lions' den is not enough to testify that a man died, but falling into a pit full of snakes and scorpions is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: If he fell into a lions' den, they do not testify about him. If he fell into a pit full of snakes and scorpions, they do testify about him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with two more cases of a man who may have died. In one case witnesses may say he died, and in the other they may not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This continues the question of when we can be sure a husband is dead so his wife may remarry. Seeing him fall into a lions' den is not enough, because lions do not always kill. A pit full of snakes and scorpions is treated as certain death, so witnesses may testify that he died.

keyTerms.meaning: We testify about him, meaning witnesses may say he died

steps.confusionAlert: "מעידין עליו" does not mean testifying about what he did. It means testifying that he is dead, which lets his wife remarry.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
If he fell into a lions' den,
they do not testify about him.
If he fell into a pit full of snakes and scorpions,
they do testify about him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from people lost at sea to other dangerous places a man might fall into.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Falling into a lions' den: no testimony that he died. Falling into a pit of snakes and scorpions: testimony that he died is allowed.

steps.title: רבי יהודה בן בתירא: not even the snake pit
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה בן בתירא disagrees and says witnesses may not testify even when a man fell into a pit of snakes and scorpions, because we are worried about something.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה בן בתירא says: Even if he fell into a pit full of snakes and scorpions, they do not testify about him, because we are concerned...
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion in the same ברייתא argues with the second case. The sentence stops just as he begins to give his reason, so the גמרא is setting up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion treated the snake pit as certain death. רבי יהודה בן בתירא says it is not certain, so it is like the lions' den. The word חיישינן tells us he has a specific worry, but the text has not said what it is yet.

keyTerms.meaning: Even, meaning this case is also included
We are concerned, meaning we take a possibility seriously

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira says:
Even if he fell into a pit full of snakes and scorpions,
they do not testify about him,
because we are concerned

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתֵירָא אוֹמֵר: אַף לַחֲפוּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the second case of the ברייתא's first opinion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even after a fall into a pit of snakes and scorpions, witnesses may not testify that he died, because of a concern that will be explained next.
